memory_candidates: When a hard-mode plan declares per-substep Commit Mode for a phase but both sub-phase edits (e.g. a deletion + a follow-on docstring rewrite touching the same file) were drafted together in one working session, reconstruct the intermediate commit boundary by restoring the file from HEAD, re-applying only the earlier sub-phase's edit, verifying it independently builds green, and committing that before layering the later sub-phase's edit back on top -- rather than trying to split one already-combined diff with git add -p.

When a plan's Definition of Done requires repo-wide 'lake lint'/'lake shake' green but the repo carries pre-existing, out-of-scope lint/shake debt in files the task's own file-boundary constraints forbid touching, treat the requirement as scoped to the task's own file set: verify zero new findings within scope, document the pre-existing repo-wide findings honestly (with counts and file lists) in the plan/summary/handoff, and do not either silently claim full-repo green or block task completion on out-of-scope debt.
